text:
morgan: Morning folks — quick async: kernel warmup sweep today. TL;DR: finishing microbatch slot allocator changes, need KV eviction policy signoff, and will run perf bench at 11:30 PT. Anyone on perf infra duty?

ben: I'm on perf infra today, can take the bench. What seq lengths / batch mixes are we running?

morgan: Planning two runs — short (512 / 1k) and long (8k). Focus is comparing batch-packing vs slot-steal under realistic arrival mix. I'll push the allocator patch to PR #423 in a few.

carol: Saw the PR diff, left one comment about that atomic counter in the slot allocator — might cause extra cache-line contention. Can we use per-shard counters + occasional aggregation?

ben: Good call. I can run quick microbench with and without the atomic to see the difference. Also will try disabling prefetch for the long run to isolate its effect.

deployer-bot: scheduled perf job 6177779950 queued (bench-runner:v2).

morgan: One blocker: need decision on KV eviction policy. Current options: LRU or TTL-prefetch hybrid for prefix caching. If we stick with plain LRU, high-cardinality keys (chat contexts) may thrash under bursty traffic.

dave: My vote is TTL-prefetch hybrid. TTL short (eg 30s) for convo prefixes + proactive prefetch on hot keys. Ops: is this a pure config change?

carol: That should be a config change plus the prefetch hook enabled in the runtime. For Dedicated nodes we'll want a canary rollout (10%) before global.

morgan: OK — canary 10% + rollback flag sounds good. Ben — please run the perf job, post the heap/cpu and per-token latency p50/p95. If the allocator diff fixes slot contention and TTL-prefetch reduces thrash, we'll merge after addressing the atomic comment. :thumbsup:

ben: Will start the runs at 11:30 PT and paste results here. Copying @dave so he can prepare the canary config.

dave: On it — I'll prepare the config map and add the canary marker. Ping me if the bench shows regression.

morgan: Thanks all. Small follow-up: if bench shows >5% tail increase on the long run, we'll rollback the allocator change and iterate. Otherwise merge + canary.
